curriculum.subject: English Language Activities
curriculum.strand: Language use 3.3.1 Verb ‘to have’ – present form
curriculum.outcomeText: select the present form of the verb ‘to have’ (have, has) and the objective pronouns (me, her/him, it) from a text

interactions.prompt: Read: I have a red ball. Tap the special word that tells ownership.
interactions.feedback: Yes! Have tells that I own the ball.

interactions.prompt: Read: Asha has a kite. Select the present form of to have.
interactions.feedback: Correct! We use has with Asha.
interactions.retryHint: Find the word between Asha and a kite.

interactions.prompt: Read: Mum calls me. Select the objective pronoun.
interactions.feedback: Great! Me receives the action in this sentence.

interactions.prompt: Read: Kamau sees her at the market. Select the objective pronoun.
interactions.feedback: Well spotted! Her is the objective pronoun.
interactions.retryHint: Choose the small word used instead of a girl's name.

interactions.prompt: Read: The goat has grass. Otieno feeds it. Which two target words appear?
interactions.feedback: Excellent! Has is a form of to have, and it is an objective pronoun.
interactions.retryHint: Find one ownership word and one word replacing the goat.

interactions.prompt: Which sentence contains have or has and an objective pronoun?
choices: I have a book; Dad reads it.
interactions.answer: I have a book; Dad reads it.
interactions.feedback: Super! You selected both have and it from the text.
interactions.retryHint: Look for an ownership word and me, her, him, or it.
